title: Week 3 trending adds: where the waiver money is going
excerpt: Sleeper's platform-wide add counts for week 3. Terrance Ferguson, Malik Washington and Xavier Hutchinson are the most claimed players of the last 24 hours, and the gap between the top of the board and the bottom is the part worth acting on.
author: FSN Desk
bodyHtml:
The most added players in the last 24 hours

Sleeper publishes how many leagues across its entire platform added each player, and these are those counts as they stand for week 3 of the 2026 season. Read them as demand, not as value. A name at the top of this list is being chased in every league at once, which is exactly when a claim costs more than the player is worth. The names further down carry the same information at a price somebody will still take.

1. Terrance Ferguson, TE, LAR

Added in 631,128 leagues in the last 24 hours. Listed first on the LAR depth chart at TE. In a second NFL season.

2. Malik Washington, WR, MIA

Added in 286,440 leagues in the last 24 hours. Listed first on the MIA depth chart at WR.

3. Xavier Hutchinson, WR, HOU

Added in 225,148 leagues in the last 24 hours. Listed first on the HOU depth chart at WR.

4. Emmett Johnson, RB, KC

Added in 222,795 leagues in the last 24 hours. Listed second on the KC depth chart at RB. A rookie, in a first NFL season.

5. Isaiah Williams, WR, NYJ

Added in 194,298 leagues in the last 24 hours.

6. Ollie Gordon, RB, MIA

Added in 177,023 leagues in the last 24 hours. Listed second on the MIA depth chart at RB. In a second NFL season.

7. Darren Waller, TE, CAR

Added in 148,635 leagues in the last 24 hours. Listed first on the CAR depth chart at TE.

8. Sam Darnold, QB, SEA

Added in 134,298 leagues in the last 24 hours. Listed first on the SEA depth chart at QB.

How to read the board

The gap between the first name and the last one is the useful number here. Terrance Ferguson at 631,128 adds and the bottom of this list at 134,298 are not the same kind of claim, even though both are trending. The first is a bidding war and the second is a quiet add, and in a league where everyone is looking at the same public counts, the quiet add is usually where the margin is.

These counts cover every league on the platform, not yours. A player already rostered in your league is noise on this board no matter how hard the rest of the platform is chasing the name. Start from the list, then check your own wire.

Source: Sleeper public API, add counts over the last 24 hours.
